text:
**My pick for most people is the JBL Charge 6.** It's the top choice at What Hi-Fi and BestProducts, and iTechGuides also names it best overall.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: JBL Charge 6.** It's IP68-rated, with about 20 hours of battery (up to 28 with Playtime Boost) and it can charge your phone. Prices run about $130 at Walmart to $150 at Amazon. [Buy links at What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) (also reviewed at [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)).
- **Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4.** It's IP67, floats, gives 360-degree sound and lasts up to 14 hours. It was about $65 at BestProducts, which also lists Amazon, Walmart and Lowe's as sellers. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Best for a pool party: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS ranks it the best waterproof speaker it has tested. It floats, can be submerged for long periods and runs over 40 hours. Its sound is directional, so it's best placed facing the crowd. It's pricey and heavy, and RTINGS doesn't list a price. [RTINGS, with Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart links](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Mid-range alternative: Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM.** It's IP67, floats and has 360-degree sound, so it sounds the same wherever you sit. Battery life is about 15 hours. Tom's Guide picks it as best overall. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) · [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Most portable: JBL Grip.** It's about the size of a soda can and under a pound. It's IP68-rated, gives 12 hours of battery and costs about $100. The mesh body can collect sand and dust. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Big and loud for the money: Soundcore Boom 2 Plus.** It's rated IPX7, floats and puts out 100 W, with up to 20 hours at half volume. It's 3.8 kg, so it's heavy. The list price is $249.99, or $200 with code AFSC20. Dealectric says it tested the code on 2026-10-22, but checkout has the final word. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus) (an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you). Its specs conflict on Bluetooth version, 6.0 on the product page and 5.3 in the manual. [Details](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus)

**Buying tips**

- Look for IP67 or IP68 for pool and beach use. IPX7 is the minimum Good Housekeeping recommends. For sand, a rating that starts with 5 or 6 (like IP67) matters, because an "X" means dust wasn't tested.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. RTINGS suggests rinsing with fresh water after use (if the manual allows it) and letting the speaker dry before charging.
- If you want to float it in the pool, choose the Wonderboom 4, EPICBOOM, Boombox 4 or Soundcore Boom 2 Plus, which are described as floating in the sources. The sources don't say whether the Charge 6 or Grip float.

If you tell me your budget and whether it's mostly for small trips or bigger gatherings, I can narrow it to one.
